item.title: 'Life is absolutely brutal in Gaza,' says World Food Programme head
item.description: The UN's World Food Programme says 1.4 million people in Gaza are suffering acute food shortages and that funding gaps are forcing cutbacks in critical aid, despite the U.S. brokered Hamas-Israel ceasefire.
item.content:encoded: The UN's World Food Programme says 1.4 million people in Gaza are suffering acute food shortages and that funding gaps are forcing cutbacks in critical aid, despite the U.S. brokered Hamas-Israel ceasefire.

item.title: Ukraine and the U.S. are at odds over Starshield. Here's what to know
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said he believes the U.S. government is behind his military's loss of normal access to the key satellite communications service used by the Ukrainian military.

item.title: Pope Leo says he will gradually resume duties after cancer surgery
item.description: Pope Leo XIV thanked thousands of faithful in St. Peter's Square on Sunday for their prayers while he was hospitalized, and said he plans to gradually return to his usual duties.

item.title: France's Macron vows to hold accountable those who 'sought to bring down the Republic'
item.description: Police arrested at least 1,800 people across France after violent groups clashed with officers and looted shops during nationwide demonstrations that drew hundreds of thousands of people.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV leaves hospital days after lung cancer surgery
item.description: The Pope left Rome's Gemelli Hospital Saturday, days after surgery for lung cancer removed the lower lobe of his right lung. He is currently scheduled to travel to Latin America in November.

item.title: Zelenskyy urges support for new US sanctions on Russia after Trump puts them on hold
item.description: Zelenskyy described the move as unfortunate, adding it would encourage Russia to continue its assault. Trump told Congress that the pause was in the national interest but gave no further details.
